scholarships.title: Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship (GOI-IES)
scholarships.official_source: Higher Education Authority (HEA) - Government of Ireland

existing.description: The Government of Ireland International Education Scholarship supports high-calibre international students who wish to study at NFQ levels 9 or 10 (master's, postgraduate diploma or PhD) in Ireland. The programme is funded by the Government of Ireland in partnership with Irish higher education institutions and managed by the Higher Education Authority, and 60 scholarships are awarded each year for one year of full-time study. Each scholarship comprises a stipend of EUR 10,000 plus a full fee waiver from the host institution for the scholarship year. Applicants must come from outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and the UK, must already hold an offer from an eligible Irish institution, and must submit one application with proof of admission and two references through the HEA portal.
eligibility: Domiciliary of origin outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and the United Kingdom
Must first apply for admission to a master's, postgraduate diploma or PhD programme at an eligible Irish higher education institution under that institution's own admission procedures

Must hold a conditional or final offer of admission to an eligible Irish higher education institution at the time of applying, with proof of admission submitted in the relevant section of the GOI-IES application form
Students who have previously held a GOI-IES scholarship are not eligible to apply
Russian and Belarusian nationals are not eligible to apply
A maximum of one application per candidate may be submitted in the 2026 cycle
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must have a domiciliary of origin outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and the United Kingdom, must first secure admission to a master's, postgraduate diploma or PhD programme at an eligible Irish higher education institution, and must hold a conditional or final offer from that institution at the time of applying, submitting proof of admission with the GOI-IES application form. Previous GOI-IES scholars and Russian and Belarusian nationals are not eligible. One application per candidate is permitted.
benefits: Full tuition fee waiver at the host institution for the scholarship year
coverage: Stipend of EUR 10,000 for one year of full-time study at NFQ levels 9 or 10
Full fee waiver from the host higher education institution for the year of the scholarship
requirements: Read the call documentation carefully to ascertain eligibility
Apply for admission to the chosen institution first and secure a conditional or final offer
Enquire directly with the relevant higher education institution about whether the intended course is eligible for GOI-IES
Submit the application through the GOI-IES online application portal
Upload two references through the portal
Submit well before the deadline to avoid technical issues caused by heavy server traffic on the deadline day
documents: Proof of admission (conditional or final offer) from the eligible Irish higher education institution, submitted in the relevant section of the application form
Two references uploaded by the applicant via the online portal
existing.english_requirement: Not specified on the official page; admission requirements are set by the individual Irish higher education institution.
application_method: Apply for admission to an eligible Irish higher education institution under its own procedures
Submit one GOI-IES application through the online application portal, with proof of admission and two references
Applications are shared with the relevant higher education institutions, which check eligibility and shortlist against their institutional strategic objectives
Shortlisted applications are assessed by an independent panel of assessors
existing.selection_notes: Applicants are expected to demonstrate a record of outstanding academic achievement, excellent communication skills, participation in extracurricular activities such as humanitarian work, politics, arts or sport, and a strong rationale for pursuing study in Ireland aligned with their longer-term goals. Institutions shortlist against their own strategic objectives before an independent panel assesses. Applications cannot be submitted once the deadline has passed and no alterations can be made after submission.
existing.best_fit: High-calibre international postgraduate students including Bangladeshi applicants
existing.duration: One year of full-time study at NFQ level 9 or 10
existing.application_period: The 2026 cycle ran to a 5pm (Irish time) deadline on 12 March 2026 with the call outcome in early June 2026. Sixty scholarships are awarded each year, so the programme is annual and the 2027 date had not been published when checked.
existing.deadline_display: 2026 Application deadline: 5pm (Irish time) 12 March 2026. The 2026 call is closed.
existing.program_type: National government scholarship for international study at NFQ levels 9 and 10, delivered in partnership with Irish higher education institutions

scholarships.title: Trinity Global Excellence Undergraduate Scholarship
scholarships.official_source: Trinity College Dublin, The University of Dublin

existing.description: Trinity's Global Excellence Undergraduate Scholarships are awarded to exceptional international students who have received a course offer for a full-time undergraduate degree at Trinity College Dublin. Scholarships range in value between EUR 2,000 and EUR 5,000 depending on the region and are applied as a reduction to the year one tuition fees of a full-time undergraduate programme. Applicants must have non-EU fee status and hold an offer to commence year one in 2026/2027; medicine, dentistry, acting, engineering, natural sciences, and computer science and statistics courses are exempt, and students from China are not eligible and should apply for the Claddagh Undergraduate Scholarship instead. Applications are made online, assessed and awarded on a rolling basis, and awards take regional and programme diversity into account.
eligibility: Must have non-EU fee status, with tuition fees billed at a non-EU rate
Must hold a course offer to commence year one of a full-time undergraduate degree programme at Trinity College Dublin for academic year 2026/2027
Medicine, dentistry, acting, engineering, natural sciences, and computer science and statistics courses are exempt from this scholarship programme
Students from China are not eligible to apply for the Global Excellence Scholarship and are directed to the Claddagh Undergraduate Scholarship instead
Awardees are expected to fully accept their course offer in order to receive the award
existing.eligibility_summary: Open to exceptional international students with non-EU fee status whose tuition fees are billed at a non-EU rate and who hold a course offer to commence year one of a full-time undergraduate degree programme at Trinity College Dublin for academic year 2026/2027. Medicine, dentistry, acting, engineering, natural sciences, and computer science and statistics courses are exempt from the programme. Students from China are not eligible.
benefits: Tuition fee reduction of EUR 2,000 to EUR 5,000 depending on region
Applied directly to the year one tuition fee bill
coverage: Reduction to the year one tuition fees of a full-time undergraduate programme
Value ranges from EUR 2,000 to EUR 5,000 depending on the region
requirements: Have non-EU fee status with tuition billed at a non-EU rate
Hold a course offer to commence year one of a full-time undergraduate degree at Trinity for the relevant academic year
Apply online using the Trinity Global Excellence Undergraduate Scholarships form
Apply early - awards are assessed on a rolling basis
Fully accept the course offer to receive the award
documents: A statement discussing how you will contribute to the Trinity College Dublin community
existing.english_requirement: Not specified on the official page; academic entry requirements are set by Trinity for each programme.
application_method: Online application using the form on the scholarship page
Provide basic personal information, secondary/high school academic results and a community contribution statement
If the online form is inaccessible in your region, contact the Trinity Regional Manager/Advisor for an alternative application form
Awards are applied to the tuition fee bills of awardees
existing.selection_notes: Applications are assessed and awarded on a rolling basis. Selection is based on academic achievement and applicants' potential to contribute to the Trinity community, and allocations also consider regional and programme diversity. Successful applicants are contacted shortly after their regional closing date; if no communication is received, the application should be assumed unsuccessful. Due to the high volume of applications, Trinity is unable to contact unsuccessful applicants individually.
existing.best_fit: Exceptional international undergraduate applicants to Trinity College Dublin
existing.duration: Year one of a full-time undergraduate programme - the award is applied as a reduction to year one tuition fees only
existing.application_period: The 2026/27 cycle closed on a rolling basis with regional deadlines running from 1 April to 15 July 2026. The scheme is annual for students starting a full-time undergraduate degree at Trinity in September.
existing.deadline_display: Regional final deadlines for 2026/27: Central, North and South America 1 April 2026; Africa 1 May 2026; all other regions 15 June 2026; South East Asia and Oceania 15 July 2026. Early application is advised and awards are made on a rolling basis.
existing.program_type: University-funded undergraduate tuition fee reduction awarded on a rolling basis by region
